## Tentative Project Title

**Liver Cancer Care Before and During the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Comparative Analysis of Clinical Presentation, Treatment Patterns, and Survival Outcomes**

## Group Members

- **Xinwen Guo (xg2489):** statistical programming and modeling
- **Yutong Li (yl6371):** data analysis, interpretation of statistical results, and written report
- **Ziang Zhang (zz3593):** website development, programming, and data cleaning

All members will review each other's code and contribute to the final report and screencast.

## Motivation

Our interest in this project stems from our undergraduate backgrounds in pharmacy and applied mathematics. Building on Yutong's previous research experience in liver cancer, we hope to apply statistical and data science methods to clinically meaningful questions. Liver cancer remains a major global health challenge, and understanding the factors associated with patient outcomes is of particular interest to us. The COVID-19 pandemic introduced additional challenges to cancer care, raising concerns about disruptions in diagnosis, treatment, and survival. These concerns motivated us to explore how liver cancer care differed before and during the pandemic.

## Intended Final Products

An R Markdown website with interactive visualizations, key findings, and the full report; a Shiny app for exploring survival by subgroup; a two-minute screencast; and a GitHub repository with all code.

## Anticipated Data Sources

We plan to use the *COVID-19 Effect on Liver Cancer Prediction Dataset*, publicly available on Kaggle:
https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/fedesoriano/covid19-effect-on-liver-cancer-prediction-dataset

The data was prospectively collected on all patients referred to the Newcastle-upon-Tyne NHS Foundation Trust (NUTH) hepatopancreatobiliary multidisciplinary team (HPB MDT) in the first 12 months of the pandemic (March 2020-February 2021), comparing to a retrospective observational cohort of consecutive patients presenting in the 12 months immediately preceding it (March 2019-February 2020). All new cases with a diagnosis of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) or intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC) confirmed radiologically or histologically, following international guidelines, were included.

The dataset contains 450 patient records and 27 variables, including demographic characteristics, cancer staging, diagnostic and treatment information, and survival outcomes.

## Planned Analysis / Visualization / Coding Challenges

We will ask whether clinical presentation, treatment patterns and timing, and survival differed between the two periods.

- **Wrangling and EDA:** clean and recode variables (`janitor`, `forcats`); compare cohorts with descriptive tables, using functions and `purrr::map` to run tests across variables; `ggplot2` and `plotly` figures
- **Regression:** logistic regression for treatment type and linear models for time to treatment, adjusting for age, sex, cancer type, and stage; cross validation to compare models; bootstrapping for confidence intervals
- **Survival analysis:** Kaplan–Meier curves with log-rank tests and Cox proportional hazards models
- **Challenges:** differing staging systems for the two cancer types, missing data, a small sample, and deploying the Shiny app
